works.title: The Fool Was Me
works.description:
Sometimes, the greatest mistake is not having a good heart, but believing that everyone else has one, too. We trust the stories, believe the tears, and offer compassion without questioning what lies beneath the surface. But appearances deceive, and even the most convincing act can hide a different reality.

Let this be a reminder: never trust blindly, never mistake a compelling story for the truth, and never let sympathy silence your instincts. Question what you are told, look beyond what you are shown, and remember that not everyone deserves your trust simply because they ask for it.

Keep your heart kind, but your eyes open. 🎭

works.title: LEGS #0910
works.description:
This artwork is part of LEGS, a collection of 170 unique 1/1 artworks created with my procedural image-generation algorithm.

LEGS explores how far the human figure can be simplified while still preserving movement, emotion, and narrative. Our perception needs surprisingly little to recognize a movement, a situation, or the relationship between figures and objects. Even when the body is reduced to basic geometric forms, we instinctively begin to see gestures, interactions, and fragments of familiar scenes.

I describe the visual language of the collection as Algorithmic Neo-Geo Assemblage. Geometric divisions, intense colors, varied patterns, grids, and simplified leg-like forms are combined into abstract compositions. Variations in structure, visual density, the number and placement of the legs, and their color relationships allow each output to suggest a different situation.

LEGS was created using my procedural image-generation algorithm, built around a set of visual rules that determine the structure and complexity of the grid, its divisions, color palettes, patterns and textures, as well as the number, form, color, and placement of the simplified leg-like figures and geometric elements.

Using controlled variation, the algorithm combines these elements to create a wide range of unique compositions. However, the final selection of artworks was made personally by me - it was neither automatic nor random.

I reviewed the outputs individually and selected the works in which I could perceive a particular movement, emotion, situation, or fragment of a narrative. Each of the 170 artworks was personally chosen by me and became part of the collection because of the story or association I discovered within its abstract forms.

The artworks are conceived as tiny stories from our lives, captured through algorithmic abstraction. Each composition acts like a film still: an intentionally cropped fragment of a larger scene. The elements are not always perfectly staged within the frame. Some are shifted, concentrated in one area, or deliberately cut off, creating a sense of movement and suggesting that something continues beyond what we can see.

Each artwork includes four traits:

Grid: Clean, Balanced, or Rich
Defines the structure and complexity of the grid composition, including the number of sections and divisions and its overall visual density.

Legs: Numeric value
Indicates the number of abstract legs within the selected output.

Leg Body Colors: Numeric value
Indicates the number of distinct colors used for the leg bodies within the selected output.

Artist Note: Personal association
Provides my personal note describing the visual association, impression, or idea that influenced my selection of the output.

Every artwork has a unique number used as its title. The Artist Note does not define the only possible meaning of the work. It offers my own perspective while leaving space for every viewer to discover a different movement, situation, or story within the same abstract forms.

MORE INFO: https://legs.neuralartistry.art/
LEGS is a collection by neuralartistry.art

works.title: Road To Marfa
works.description:
Road To Marfa

A journey into the strange, the distant, and the symbolic. Somewhere in the vast Texas desert, a storefront stands alone, blurring the lines between art, commerce, and culture.

This piece is my way of being part of Marfa from afar. While I may not be there physically, my art will be. A small gesture of presence, a road leading somewhere between the real and the imagined.

Sometimes, being there in spirit is enough.

works.description:
Dragon of the Sky  
Efdot × Luko, 2026

The sky was painting itself orange again, but this time it felt different. The clouds turned into swirling creatures that told us to paint.

Efdot and Luko collaborated at the Rio Art Residency in July 2024, each mark answering the last. The blobs locked together like scales. Now they dance around an eternal fire.

Animated painting, 16-second looping MP4

works.title: Unnumbered Tears
works.description:
acrylic on canvas, 100*70 CM, 2026



A bird sits on a dead branch.

That bird is me.

I am neither a hero nor a victim. I do not run away, and I do not have the power to intervene. I cannot stop the catastrophe, nor can I bring back what has already been lost.

This work is not about war; it is about the painful distance between seeing and acting.

While creating this work, I kept thinking about the words Francisco Goya wrote beneath one of the prints in The Disasters of War:

“Yo lo vi.” (“I saw this.”)

This work is also an attempt to capture that same moment: the moment when a person stands before catastrophe and can no longer look away.

I saw this.

works.title: Midas Curse
works.description:
The Artwork captures the final solitude of a man imprisoned by his own desires.
Once a king who sought gold above all else, Midas now stands alone — abandoned by power, stripped of meaning.

The artwork shows him swallowed by darkness, with nothing left to see but his own reflection in gold. His body is bound, his feet no longer free to conquer but held in place by the weight of his choices. A sword runs through him—a final, silent judgment that even kings are not spared from ruin.

Midas, in his last moments, is frozen between life and death — a figure of agony, regret, and inevitable downfall.
He reached the pinnacle of wealth, only to find himself utterly alone, betrayed by the very gold he once worshipped.

works.title: CONTEMPLATING DEATH: MUHJU
works.description: Contemplating Death" is a thought-provoking and visually enthralling artwork that delves into the enigmatic nature of life, death, and the eternal cycle of existence. The piece features an angel, sitting atop an ornately decorated Greek temple. The angel's foot is dipped into the vast cosmic expanse, which remains constant in the background. The observer witnesses the angel's transformation from a pure white form into a striking black silhouette, representing its fusion with the universe. This metamorphosis occurs in cycles, with the angel reverting to its white form, symbolizing rebirth and renewal. The angel's appearance changes according to the time of day, with its white form appearing during daylight hours and its dark form emerging at night.
